title: AI-supported planning and skull-implant design in the separation of craniopagus twins Mercy and Goodness
summary: PureHealth/SKMC statement (5 June 2026) cites “AI-enhanced surgical planning”; XRlabs' own release claims AI-designed implants. The twins were separated in four operations and returned to Nigeria.
account: PureHealth reported on June 5, 2026 that surgeons at Sheikh Khalifa Medical City in Abu Dhabi had separated Nigerian twins Mercy and Goodness. More than 60 clinicians took part in four staged procedures, led by Noor ul Owase Jeelani of Gemini Untwined. The hospital credited AI-assisted planning, mixed reality, and custom titanium skull grafts. On June 19, XRlabs identified its implant-design platform and said that its model used infant head shapes to generate patient-specific implants from CT data. The company also described surgical rehearsal in a shared virtual environment and reported that the twins had returned home. These are accounts from the treating institution and technology supplier. They establish a claimed AI contribution to a successful surgical procedure, without measuring how much AI improved the result. The reports differ on age and timing, and do not provide an exact operation date.
purpose: XRlabs says its platform is built to design patient-specific implants and plan operations in mixed reality. The hospital's “AI-enhanced surgical planning” is described only generically. Implant design for this separation was the vendor's stated purpose.
system: XRlabs 'Surgical Intelligence' platform for AI-designed skull implants (identified only by the vendor) and unnamed 'AI-enhanced surgical planning' (PureHealth statement)
developer: XRlabs (implant design, per its own release); the hospital names no developer for the planning tools
deployer: PureHealth - SEHA Sheikh Khalifa Medical City, Abu Dhabi, with Gemini Untwined (Professor Noor Ul Owase Jeelani)
domain: Healthcare - pediatric neurosurgery and craniofacial surgery
segment: Craniopagus twin separation: surgical planning and patient-specific implants
taxonomy_note: The AI's claimed part is surgical planning; the good recorded is the twins' separation.

ratings.reason: Two children joined at the head were separated, reconstructed and discharged home to Nigeria, per the hospital and press. The surgical team produced this outcome, and no source quantifies the AI's share of it.
XRlabs claims that implant design took seconds, but supplies no measured comparison with manual design or independently verified planning-time saving.

Neither provides a comparison without AI or a clinical evaluation that separates the model’s contribution from the surgical team’s work.

fields.account: PureHealth reported on June 5, 2026 that surgeons at Sheikh Khalifa Medical City in Abu Dhabi had separated Nigerian twins Mercy and Goodness. More than 60 clinicians took part in four staged procedures, led by Noor ul Owase Jeelani of Gemini Untwined. The hospital credited AI-assisted planning, mixed reality, and custom titanium skull grafts. On June 19, XRlabs identified its implant-design platform and said that its model used infant head shapes to generate patient-specific implants from CT data. The company also described surgical rehearsal in a shared virtual environment and reported that the twins had returned home. These are accounts from the treating institution and technology supplier. They establish a claimed AI contribution to a successful surgical procedure, without measuring how much AI improved the result. The reports differ on age and timing, and do not provide an exact operation date.

fields.account: PureHealth reported on June 5, 2026 that surgeons at Sheikh Khalifa Medical City in Abu Dhabi had separated Nigerian twins Mercy and Goodness. More than 60 clinicians took part in four staged procedures, led by Noor ul Owase Jeelani of Gemini Untwined. The hospital credited AI-assisted planning, mixed reality, and custom titanium skull grafts. On June 19, XRlabs identified its implant-design platform and said that its model used infant head shapes to generate patient-specific implants from CT data. The company also described surgical rehearsal in a shared virtual environment and reported that the twins had returned home. These are accounts from the treating institution and technology supplier. They establish a claimed AI contribution to a successful surgical procedure, without measuring how much AI improved the result. The reports differ on age and timing, and do not provide an exact operation date.

produced_by: A multidisciplinary surgical team performing four staged procedures
CT-derived 3D models, mixed-reality rehearsal, and patient-specific skull implants
Specialist coordination by Gemini Untwined and the treating hospital
must_hold: A surgical team able to act on AI-assisted plans and patient-specific implants
Imaging of sufficient quality to model the twins' shared vasculature and skull
The vendor's claims about the implant-design AI are not independently documented, so the AI's share cannot be assumed to transfer
